clues: This city stands on the shore of the Ligurian Sea. It is in north Tuscany, in Italy, and is the next biggest town after Lucca.
Mountains close to the coast help make its summers humid and rainy. Strong south-east winds batter the shore and cause severe storms for days at a time.
The tower Torre Matilde was built in 1541 by the people of Lucca to fight off sea raiders. It is still the oldest building in town.
For its big carnival, huge papier-mâché floats parade along the sea front in party weeks. The carnival has run since the year 1873.
Burlamacco is the mask of its carnival. He was first made in 1930 and is its true sign.
